clusters.pick_reason: #2763 ships a changeset bumping core-internal/client/server and explicitly documents the new semantics: the pending timer now arms for whichever of timeout/maxTotalTimeout comes first, progress resets re-arm against the remaining budget (not the full per-request timeout), and cap expiry raises a distinct 'Maximum total timeout exceeded' error - this covers the same progress-reset code path #2817 touches, but ties it to the maxTotalTimeout cap. #2817 has no changeset and only adds info.startTime = Date.now() on every progress reset with no accompanying maxTotalTimeout accounting; it only edits an existing test's comment rather than adding new coverage. clusters.pick_reason: #2763 ships a changeset bumping core-internal/client/server and explicitly documents the new semantics: the pending timer now arms for whichever of timeout/maxTotalTimeout comes first, progress resets re-arm against the remaining budget (not the full per-request timeout), and cap expiry raises a distinct 'Maximum total timeout exceeded' error - this covers the same progress-reset code path #2817 touches, but ties it to the maxTotalTimeout cap. #2817 has no changeset and only adds info.startTime = Date.now() on every progress reset with no accompanying maxTotalTimeout accounting; it only edits an existing test's comment rather than adding new coverage. Unconditionally resetting startTime on each progress notification (2817's approach) would let a peer bypass a maxTotalTimeout cap indefinitely via periodic progress pings, which conflicts with the hard-cap guarantee #2763 introduces for the same code region.
